questions.text: Let $A=\{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ and $B=\{1, 4, 9, 16\}$. Then the number of many-one functions $f:A\to B$ such that $1\in f(A)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Functions $A\to B$ whose range contains 1: $4^4-3^4=256-81=175$.
The one-one functions (bijections, $4!=24$) all contain 1 in the range and must be excluded.
Many-one functions: $175-24=151$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $\alpha_\theta$ and $\beta_\theta$ be the distinct roots of $2x^2+(\cos\theta)x-1=0$, $\theta\in(0, 2\pi)$. If m and M are the minimum and the maximum values of $\alpha_\theta^4+\beta_\theta^4$, then $16(M+m)$ equals :
questions.sol:
$\alpha+\beta=-\dfrac{\cos\theta}{2}$, $\alpha\beta=-\dfrac12$, so $\alpha^2+\beta^2=\dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{4}+1$.
$\alpha^4+\beta^4=\left(1+\dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{4}\right)^2-\dfrac12$, with $\cos^2\theta\in[0, 1]$.
$m=1-\dfrac12=\dfrac12$, $M=\dfrac{25}{16}-\dfrac12=\dfrac{17}{16}$.
$16(M+m)=17+8=25$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the curve $z(1+i)+\bar{z}(1-i)=4$, $z\in\mathbf{C}$, divide the region $|z-3|\le1$ into two parts of areas $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Then $|\alpha-\beta|$ equals :
questions.sol:
With $z=x+iy$: $z(1+i)+\bar z(1-i)=2(x-y)=4$, the line $x-y=2$.
The disc has centre $(3, 0)$, radius 1; the distance of the centre from the line is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$, so the chord subtends a right angle at the centre.
Minor segment $=\dfrac12\left(\dfrac\pi2-1\right)=\dfrac\pi4-\dfrac12$; major part $=\pi-\left(\dfrac\pi4-\dfrac12\right)$.
$|\alpha-\beta|=\pi-2\left(\dfrac\pi4-\dfrac12\right)=1+\dfrac\pi2$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text:
If the system of linear equations :
$x+y+2z=6$,
$2x+3y+az=a+1$,
$-x-3y+bz=2b$,
where $a, b\in\mathbf{R}$, has infinitely many solutions, then $7a+3b$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Eliminating $x$: (2nd) $-2$(1st) gives $y+(a-4)z=a-11$; (3rd) $+$ (1st) gives $-2y+(b+2)z=2b+6$.
Adding twice the first of these: $(2a+b-6)z=2a+2b-16$.
Infinitely many solutions need $2a+b-6=0$ and $2a+2b-16=0$: $a=-2$, $b=10$.
$7a+3b=-14+30=16$.

questions.text: For a $3\times3$ matrix M, let trace (M) denote the sum of all the diagonal elements of M. Let A be a $3\times3$ matrix such that $|A|=\dfrac{1}{2}$ and trace $(A)=3$. If $B=\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}(2A))$, then the value of $|B|+$ trace $(B)$ equals :
questions.sol:
For order 3, $\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}M)=|M|M$. Here $|2A|=8\cdot\dfrac12=4$, so $B=4(2A)=8A$.
$|B|=8^3\cdot\dfrac12=256$ and trace $(B)=8\times3=24$.
Sum $=280$.

questions.text: Suppose that the number of terms in an A.P. is $2k$, $k\in\mathbf{N}$. If the sum of all odd terms of the A.P. is 40, the sum of all even terms is 55 and the last term of the A.P. exceeds the first term by 27, then k is equal to :
questions.sol:
Each even term exceeds the odd term before it by $d$, and there are $k$ such pairs: $kd=55-40=15$.
Last $-$ first $=(2k-1)d=27$, i.e. $2kd-d=27$, so $d=3$.
$k=5$.

questions.text: In a group of 3 girls and 4 boys, there are two boys $B_1$ and $B_2$. The number of ways, in which these girls and boys can stand in a queue such that all the girls stand together, all the boys stand together, but $B_1$ and $B_2$ are not adjacent to each other, is :
questions.sol:
The girls' block and the boys' block can be in 2 orders; the girls can be arranged in $3!=6$ ways.
Boys with $B_1$, $B_2$ not adjacent: $4!-2\cdot3!=24-12=12$.
Total $=2\times6\times12=144$.

questions.text:
Let $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\delta$ be the coefficients of $x^7$, $x^5$, $x^3$ and $x$ respectively in the expansion of $\left(x+\sqrt{x^3-1}\right)^5+\left(x-\sqrt{x^3-1}\right)^5$, $x>1$. If u and v satisfy the equations
$\alpha u+\beta v=18$,
$\gamma u+\delta v=20$,
then $u+v$ equals :
questions.sol:
The odd powers of $\sqrt{x^3-1}$ cancel: the sum is $2\left[x^5+10x^3(x^3-1)+5x(x^3-1)^2\right]=10x^7+20x^6+2x^5-20x^4-20x^3+10x$.
$\alpha=10$, $\beta=2$, $\gamma=-20$, $\delta=10$.
$10u+2v=18$ and $-20u+10v=20$ give $u=1$, $v=4$; $u+v=5$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If A and B are two events such that $P(A\cap B)=0.1$, and $P(A\mid B)$ and $P(B\mid A)$ are the roots of the equation $12x^2-7x+1=0$, then the value of $\dfrac{P(\bar{A}\cup\bar{B})}{P(\bar{A}\cap\bar{B})}$ is :
questions.sol:
The roots are $\dfrac13$ and $\dfrac14$. Since $P(A\mid B)=\dfrac{0.1}{P(B)}$ and $P(B\mid A)=\dfrac{0.1}{P(A)}$, $P(A)$ and $P(B)$ are 0.3 and 0.4.
$P(\bar A\cup\bar B)=1-P(A\cap B)=0.9$.
$P(\bar A\cap\bar B)=1-P(A\cup B)=1-(0.7-0.1)=0.4$.
Ratio $=\dfrac{0.9}{0.4}=\dfrac94$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $P\left(4, 4\sqrt{3}\right)$ be a point on the parabola $y^2=4ax$ and PQ be a focal chord of the parabola. If M and N are the foot of perpendiculars drawn from P and Q respectively on the directrix of the parabola, then the area of the quadrilateral PQMN is equal to :
questions.sol:
$48=16a$, so $a=3$ and P has parameter $t=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}$. The other end of the focal chord has parameter $-\dfrac1t=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$: $Q\left(\dfrac94, -3\sqrt3\right)$.
Directrix $x=-3$: $PM=7$, $QN=\dfrac{21}{4}$, and $MN=4\sqrt3+3\sqrt3=7\sqrt3$.
PQNM is a trapezium: area $=\dfrac12\left(7+\dfrac{21}{4}\right)7\sqrt3=\dfrac{343\sqrt3}{8}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $E:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, $a>b$ and $H:\dfrac{x^2}{A^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{B^2}=1$. Let the distance between the foci of E and the foci of H be $2\sqrt{3}$. If $a-A=2$, and the ratio of the eccentricities of E and H is $\dfrac{1}{3}$, then the sum of the lengths of their latus rectums is equal to :
questions.sol:
Read as: the distance between the two foci is $2\sqrt3$ for each curve, i.e. $ae=Ae'=\sqrt3$, where $e$ and $e'=3e$ are the eccentricities of E and H.
Then $a=3A$, and $a-A=2$ gives $A=1$, $a=3$; $e=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}$, $e'=\sqrt3$.
$b^2=9\left(1-\dfrac13\right)=6$ and $B^2=1(3-1)=2$.
Latus rectums: $\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=4$ and $\dfrac{2B^2}{A}=4$; sum $=8$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The sum of all values of $\theta\in[0, 2\pi]$ satisfying $2\sin^2\theta=\cos2\theta$ and $2\cos^2\theta=3\sin\theta$ is
questions.sol:
$2\sin^2\theta=1-2\sin^2\theta$ gives $\sin^2\theta=\dfrac14$.
$2-2\sin^2\theta=3\sin\theta$ gives $(2\sin\theta-1)(\sin\theta+2)=0$, so $\sin\theta=\dfrac12$.
Both hold for $\theta=\dfrac\pi6, \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$; sum $=\pi$.

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ be two unit vectors such that the angle between them is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. If $\lambda\vec{a}+2\vec{b}$ and $3\vec{a}-\lambda\vec{b}$ are perpendicular to each other, then the number of values of $\lambda$ in $[-1, 3]$ is :
questions.sol:
$\vec a\cdot\vec b=\dfrac12$. $(\lambda\vec a+2\vec b)\cdot(3\vec a-\lambda\vec b)=3\lambda-\dfrac{\lambda^2}{2}+3-2\lambda=0$, i.e. $\lambda^2-2\lambda-6=0$.
$\lambda=1\pm\sqrt7\approx3.65$ or $-1.65$; neither lies in $[-1, 3]$.
Number of values $=0$.

questions.text: The perpendicular distance, of the line $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y+2}{-1}=\dfrac{z+3}{2}$ from the point $P(2, -10, 1)$, is :
questions.sol:
The line passes through $A(1, -2, -3)$ with unit direction $\dfrac13(2, -1, 2)$. $\vec{AP}=(1, -8, 4)$, $|\vec{AP}|^2=81$.
Projection on the line $=\dfrac{2+8+8}{3}=6$.
Distance $=\sqrt{81-36}=3\sqrt5$.

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}\left(\left(\frac{e}{1-e}\right)\left(\frac{1}{e}-\frac{x}{1+x}\right)\right)^x=\alpha$, then the value of $\dfrac{\log_e\alpha}{1+\log_e\alpha}$ equals :
questions.sol:
The base is $g(x)=\dfrac{1}{1-e}\cdot\dfrac{1+(1-e)x}{1+x}\to1$, a $1^\infty$ form.
$g(x)-1=\dfrac{e}{(1-e)(1+x)}$, so $\log_e\alpha=\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}x\,(g(x)-1)=\frac{e}{1-e}$.
$\dfrac{\log_e\alpha}{1+\log_e\alpha}=\dfrac{e/(1-e)}{1/(1-e)}=e$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^{x^2}\frac{t^2-8t+15}{e^t}\,dt$, $x\in\mathbf{R}$. Then the numbers of local maximum and local minimum points of $f$, respectively, are :
questions.sol:
$f'(x)=2x\,(x^4-8x^2+15)e^{-x^2}=2x(x^2-3)(x^2-5)e^{-x^2}$, with simple zeros at $0, \pm\sqrt3, \pm\sqrt5$.
Sign of $f'$ from left to right: $-, +, -, +, -, +$.
Minima at $-\sqrt5, 0, \sqrt5$ and maxima at $\pm\sqrt3$: 2 maxima and 3 minima.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The area of the region enclosed by the curves $y=x^2-4x+4$ and $y^2=16-8x$ is :
questions.sol:
With $u=2-x$: $y=u^2$ and $y^2=8u$. They meet at $u=0$ and $u=2$, i.e. at $(2, 0)$ and $(0, 4)$.
Area $=\displaystyle\int_0^2\left(\sqrt{8u}-u^2\right)du=\frac{16}{3}-\frac83=\frac83$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $x=f(y)$ is the solution of the differential equation $\left(1+y^2\right)+\left(x-2e^{\tan^{-1}y}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$, $y\in\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ with $f(0)=1$, then $f\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
As an equation for $x(y)$: $\dfrac{dx}{dy}+\dfrac{x}{1+y^2}=\dfrac{2e^{\tan^{-1}y}}{1+y^2}$; integrating factor $e^{\tan^{-1}y}$.
$xe^{\tan^{-1}y}=\displaystyle\int\frac{2e^{2\tan^{-1}y}}{1+y^2}dy=e^{2\tan^{-1}y}+C$, so $x=e^{\tan^{-1}y}+Ce^{-\tan^{-1}y}$.
$f(0)=1$ gives $C=0$; $f\left(\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\right)=e^{\pi/6}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\int e^x\left(\frac{x\sin^{-1}x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}+\frac{\sin^{-1}x}{(1-x^2)^{3/2}}+\frac{x}{1-x^2}\right)dx=g(x)+C$, where C is the constant of integration, then $g\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ equals :
questions.sol:
Let $h(x)=\dfrac{x\sin^{-1}x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$. Then $h'(x)=\dfrac{\sin^{-1}x}{(1-x^2)^{3/2}}+\dfrac{x}{1-x^2}$, so the integrand is $e^x(h+h')$.
$g(x)=e^xh(x)$, and $g\left(\dfrac12\right)=\sqrt e\cdot\dfrac{\frac12\cdot\frac\pi6}{\frac{\sqrt3}{2}}=\dfrac{\pi}{6}\sqrt{\dfrac e3}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $A(6, 8)$, $B(10\cos\alpha, -10\sin\alpha)$ and $C(-10\sin\alpha, 10\cos\alpha)$, be the vertices of a triangle. If $L(a, 9)$ and $G(h, k)$ be its orthocenter and centroid respectively, then $(5a-3h+6k+100\sin2\alpha)$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
All three vertices are 10 from the origin, so the circumcentre is O and the orthocentre is $A+B+C$.
$y$: $8-10\sin\alpha+10\cos\alpha=9$, so $\cos\alpha-\sin\alpha=\dfrac1{10}$; then $a=6+10(\cos\alpha-\sin\alpha)=7$.
$G=\dfrac{L}{3}=\left(\dfrac73, 3\right)$. Squaring, $1-\sin2\alpha=\dfrac1{100}$, so $100\sin2\alpha=99$.
$35-7+18+99=145$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $y=f(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{xy}{x^2-1}=\dfrac{x^6+4x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$, $-1<x<1$ such that $f(0)=0$. If $6\displaystyle\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}f(x)\,dx=2\pi-\alpha$ then $\alpha^2$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Integrating factor $e^{\int\frac{x}{x^2-1}dx}=\sqrt{1-x^2}$: $y\sqrt{1-x^2}=\displaystyle\int(x^6+4x)\,dx=\frac{x^7}{7}+2x^2$ (using $f(0)=0$).
The odd part integrates to zero: $\displaystyle\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}f=4\int_0^{1/2}\frac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}dx=4\left(\frac{\pi}{12}-\frac{\sqrt3}{8}\right)$ (put $x=\sin\theta$).
$6\times$ this $=2\pi-3\sqrt3$, so $\alpha=3\sqrt3$ and $\alpha^2=27$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the distance between two parallel lines be 5 units and a point P lie between the lines at a unit distance from one of them. An equilateral triangle PQR is formed such that Q lies on one of the parallel lines, while R lies on the other. Then $(QR)^2$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Take the lines $y=0$ and $y=5$, and $P(0, 1)$. Let side $s$ and $\vec{PQ}=s(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$ with $s\sin\theta=-1$; $R$ is obtained by turning $\vec{PQ}$ through $60^\circ$, and must have $y$-increase 4.
$s\sin(\theta+60^\circ)=\dfrac{-1}{2}+\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}s\cos\theta=4$, so $s\cos\theta=3\sqrt3$.
$s^2=1+27=28$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $A=\{1, 2, 3\}$. The number of relations on A, containing $(1, 2)$ and $(2, 3)$, which are reflexive and transitive but not symmetric, is __________.
questions.sol:
Reflexivity and transitivity force $(1,1), (2,2), (3,3)$ and $(1,3)$. The only other pairs are $(2,1)$, $(3,2)$, $(3,1)$.
Adding nothing, only $(2,1)$, or only $(3,2)$ keeps the relation transitive. Adding $(3,1)$ forces $(3,2)$ and then $(2,1)$; adding both $(2,1)$ and $(3,2)$ forces $(3,1)$, giving the full relation, which is symmetric.
Number $=3$.

questions.text: Which one of the following is the correct dimensional formula for the capacitance in F ? M, L, T and C stand for unit of mass, length, time and charge,
questions.sol:
Capacitance $=\dfrac{Q}{V}$ and $V=\dfrac{W}{Q}$ has dimensions $\mathrm{ML^2T^{-2}C^{-1}}$.
$[C]=\dfrac{\mathrm{C}}{\mathrm{ML^2T^{-2}C^{-1}}}=\mathrm{C^2M^{-1}L^{-2}T^2}$.

questions.text:
The maximum percentage error in the measurment of density of a wire is
[Given, mass of wire $=(0.60\pm0.003)$ g
radius of wire $=(0.50\pm0.01)$ cm
length of wire $=(10.00\pm0.05)$ cm]
questions.sol:
$\rho=\dfrac{m}{\pi r^2l}$, so $\dfrac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}=\dfrac{\Delta m}{m}+2\dfrac{\Delta r}{r}+\dfrac{\Delta l}{l}$.
$=0.5\%+2(2\%)+0.5\%=5\%$.

questions.text: A ball of mass 100 g is projected with velocity 20 m/s at $60^\circ$ with horizontal. The decrease in kinetic energy of the ball during the motion from point of projection to highest point is
questions.sol:
At the highest point only the vertical component of velocity is lost.
Decrease in KE $=\dfrac12m(u\sin60^\circ)^2=\dfrac12\times0.1\times\left(20\times\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2=0.05\times300=15$ J.

questions.text:
A body of mass 100 g is moving in circular path of radius 2 m on vertical plane as shown in figure. The velocity of the body at point A is 10 m/s. The ratio of its kinetic energies at point B and C is :
(Take acceleration due to gravity as 10 m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
OB makes $30^\circ$ with the downward vertical, so B is $2(1-\cos30^\circ)=2-\sqrt3$ m above A. OC is $90^\circ$ beyond OB, i.e. $60^\circ$ from the upward vertical, so C is $2(1+\cos60^\circ)=3$ m above A.
$v^2=v_A^2-2gh$: $v_B^2=100-20(2-\sqrt3)=60+20\sqrt3$, $v_C^2=100-60=40$.
$K_B:K_C=\dfrac{60+20\sqrt3}{40}=\dfrac{3+\sqrt3}{2}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A force $\vec{F}=2\hat{i}+b\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ is applied on a particle and it undergoes a displacement $\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$. What will be the value of b, if work done on the particle is zero.
questions.sol: $W=\vec F\cdot\vec d=2-2b-1=0$, so $b=\dfrac12$.

questions.text: A tube of length L is shown in the figure. The radius of cross section at the point (1) is 2 cm and at the point (2) is 1 cm, respectively. If the velocity of water entering at point (1) is 2 m/s, then velocity of water leaving the point (2) will be
questions.sol: Continuity: $A_1v_1=A_2v_2$, so $v_2=v_1\left(\dfrac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^2=2\times4=8$ m/s.

questions.text:
A small rigid spherical ball of mass M is dropped in a long vertical tube containing glycerine. The velocity of the ball becomes constant after some time. If the density of glycerine is half of the density of the ball, then the viscous force acting on the ball will be
(consider g as acceleration due to gravity)
questions.sol:
At terminal velocity the net force is zero: weight $=$ buoyancy $+$ viscous force.
Buoyancy $=\dfrac{Mg}{2}$ (liquid density is half the ball's), so the viscous force $=Mg-\dfrac{Mg}{2}=\dfrac{Mg}{2}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
For a diatomic gas, if $\gamma_1=\left(\dfrac{C_p}{C_v}\right)$ for rigid molecules and $\gamma_2=\left(\dfrac{C_p}{C_v}\right)$ for another diatomic molecules, but also having vibrational modes. Then, which one of the following options is correct ?
($C_p$ and $C_v$ are specific heats of the gas at constant pressure and volume)
questions.sol:
Rigid diatomic: $f=5$, $\gamma_1=\dfrac75$. With vibration, $f=7$, $\gamma_2=\dfrac97$.
More degrees of freedom lower $\gamma=1+\dfrac2f$, so $\gamma_2<\gamma_1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given are statements for certain thermodynamic variables,
(A) Internal energy, volume (V) and mass (M) are extensive variables.
(B) Pressure (P), temperature (T) and density ($\rho$) are intensive variables.
(C) Volume (V), temperature (T) and density ($\rho$) are intensive variables.
(D) Mass (M), temperature (T) and internal energy are extensive variables.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Extensive variables scale with the amount of matter: internal energy, volume, mass. Intensive ones do not: pressure, temperature, density.
(A) and (B) are correct; (C) wrongly calls volume intensive and (D) wrongly calls temperature extensive.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : A simple pendulum is taken to a planet of mass and radius, 4 times and 2 times, respectively, than the Earth. The time period of the pendulum remains same on earth and the planet.
Reason (R) : The mass of the pendulum remains unchanged at Earth and the other planet.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol:
$g=\dfrac{GM}{R^2}$: on the planet $g'=\dfrac{4}{2^2}g=g$, so $T=2\pi\sqrt{l/g}$ is unchanged. (A) is true.
The mass of the bob is indeed unchanged, so (R) is true, but $T$ does not depend on the mass at all; the reason for (A) is the equal value of $g$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: For a short dipole placed at origin O, the dipole moment P is along $x$-axis, as shown in the figure. If the electric potential and electric field at A are $V_0$ and $E_0$, respectively, then the correct combination of the electric potential and electric field, respectively, at point B on the $y$-axis is given by
questions.sol:
A is on the axis at distance $r$: $E_0=\dfrac{2kp}{r^3}$.
B is on the equatorial line at distance $2r$: $V=0$ and $E=\dfrac{kp}{(2r)^3}=\dfrac{kp}{8r^3}=\dfrac{E_0}{16}$.

questions.text: A rectangular metallic loop is moving out of a uniform magnetic field region to a field free region with a constant speed. When the loop is partially inside the magnate field, the plot of magnitude of induced emf $(\varepsilon)$ with time (t) is given by
questions.sol:
While the loop is leaving, only one side of length $l$ cuts the field lines, and the flux changes at a steady rate $Blv$.
So $\varepsilon=Blv$ is constant in time: graph (1).

questions.text: A series LCR circuit is connected to an alternating source of emf E. The current amplitude at resonant frequency is $I_0$. If the value of resistance R becomes twice of its initial value then amplitude of current at resonance will be
questions.sol:
At resonance the impedance equals R, so $I_0=\dfrac{E_0}{R}$.
Doubling R halves the amplitude: $\dfrac{I_0}{2}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : In Young's double slit experiment, the fringes produced by red light are closer as compared to those produced by blue light.
Reason (R) : The fringe width is directly proportional to the wavelength of light.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol:
$\beta=\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$, so fringe width is proportional to wavelength: (R) is true.
Red light has the longer wavelength, so its fringes are wider apart, not closer: (A) is false.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A transparent film of refractive index, 2.0 is coated on a glass slab of refractive index, 1.45. What is the minimum thickness of transparent film to be coated for the maximum transmission of Green light of wavelength 550 nm. [Assume that the light is incident nearly perpendicular to the glass surface.]
questions.sol:
Maximum transmission means minimum reflection. Reflection at air-film ($1\to2.0$) has a phase change of $\pi$; reflection at film-glass ($2.0\to1.45$) has none.
With one extra $\pi$, the reflected rays cancel when $2nt=m\lambda$; the least non-zero thickness is $t=\dfrac{\lambda}{2n}=\dfrac{550}{4}=137.5$ nm.

questions.text: A symmetric thin biconvex lens is cut into four equal parts by two planes AB and CD as shown in figure. If the power of original lens is 4D then the power of a part of the divided lens is
questions.sol:
The cut along AB (containing the principal axis) does not change the focal length of each piece.
The cut along CD (the plane of the lens) splits it into two identical plano-convex lenses, each with half the power: $\dfrac{4}{2}=2$ D.
Each quarter therefore has power 2D.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A light source of wavelength $\lambda$ illuminates a metal surface and electrons are ejected with maximum kinetic energy of 2 eV. If the same surface is illuminated by a light source of wavelength $\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$, then the maximum kinetic energy of ejected electrons will be (The work function of metal is 1 eV)
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}=2+1=3$ eV. Halving the wavelength doubles the photon energy to 6 eV.
$K_{max}=6-1=5$ eV.

questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: An electron projected perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B moves in a circle. If Bohr's quantization is applicable, then the radius of the electronic orbit in the first excited state is :
questions.sol:
Circular motion: $mv=eBr$. Bohr's condition: $mvr=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$.
So $eBr^2=\dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$ and $r=\sqrt{\dfrac{nh}{2\pi eB}}$.
First excited state, $n=2$: $r=\sqrt{\dfrac{h}{\pi eB}}$.

questions.text: To obtain the given truth table, following logic gate should be placed at G :
questions.note: NTA dropped this question in the final key (full marks to everyone). The answer index stored here is only a placeholder.
questions.sol:
The table gives $Y=1$ only when $A=B$, i.e. $Y=AB+\bar A\bar B$.
If the two AND gates deliver $A\bar B$ and $\bar AB$, then a NOR gate at G gives $\overline{A\bar B+\bar AB}=AB+\bar A\bar B$, matching the table.
The wiring of the drawn circuit does not clearly give these two inputs, and the question was dropped.

questions.text: A tube of length 1m is filled completely with an ideal liquid of mass 2M, and closed at both ends. The tube is rotated uniformly in horizontal plane about one of its ends. If the force exerted by the liquid at the other end is F then angular velocity of the tube is $\sqrt{\dfrac{F}{\alpha M}}$ in SI unit. The value of $\alpha$ is __________.
questions.sol:
The closed end supplies the centripetal force for the whole liquid column, whose centre of mass is at $\dfrac L2=0.5$ m.
$F=(2M)\omega^2(0.5)=M\omega^2$, so $\omega=\sqrt{\dfrac FM}$ and $\alpha=1$.

questions.text: The net current flowing in the given circuit is __________ A.
questions.sol:
In steady d.c. the capacitor branch carries no current, so everything beyond it is cut off.
The 3 $\Omega$ and the diagonal 6 $\Omega$ are in parallel ($2\ \Omega$), in series with 2 $\Omega$: $4\ \Omega$. This is in parallel with the diagonal 4 $\Omega$ across the cell: $2\ \Omega$.
Current $=\dfrac{2}{2}=1$ A.

questions.text: Two long parallel wires X and Y, separated by a distance of 6 cm, carry currents of 5A and 4A, respectively, in opposite directions as shown in the figure. Magnitude of the resultant magnetic field at point P at a distance of 4 cm from wire Y is $x\times10^{-5}$ T. The value of $x$ is __________. Take permeability of free space as $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}$ SI units.
questions.sol:
P is 10 cm from X and 4 cm from Y, on the far side of Y.
$B_X=\dfrac{\mu_0(5)}{2\pi(0.10)}=1\times10^{-5}$ T and $B_Y=\dfrac{\mu_0(4)}{2\pi(0.04)}=2\times10^{-5}$ T.
The currents are opposite, so at P the two fields are opposite: $B=1\times10^{-5}$ T, $x=1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A proton is moving undeflected in a region of crossed electric and magnetic fields at a constant speed of $2\times10^5$ m s$^{-1}$. When the electric field is switched off, the proton moves along a circular path of radius 2 cm. The magnitude of electric field is $x\times10^4$ N/C. The value of $x$ is __________. Take the mass of the proton $=1.6\times10^{-27}$ kg.
questions.sol:
$r=\dfrac{mv}{qB}$, so $B=\dfrac{1.6\times10^{-27}\times2\times10^5}{1.6\times10^{-19}\times0.02}=0.1$ T.
Undeflected motion: $E=vB=2\times10^5\times0.1=2\times10^4$ N/C, so $x=2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor of area $A=16$ cm$^2$ and separation between the plates 10 cm, is charged by a DC current. Consider a hypothetical plane surface of area $A_0=3.2$ cm$^2$ inside the capacitor and parallel to the plates. At an instant, the current through the circuit is 6A. At the same instant the displacement current through $A_0$ is __________ mA.
questions.sol:
The total displacement current between the plates equals the conduction current, 6 A, spread uniformly over the plate area.
Through $A_0$: $6\times\dfrac{3.2}{16}=1.2$ A $=1200$ mA.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : A spectral line will be observed for a $2p_x\rightarrow2p_y$ transition.
Statement (II) : $2p_x$ and $2p_y$ are degenerate orbitals.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
$2p_x$ and $2p_y$ have the same energy (degenerate), so Statement (II) is true.
A transition between orbitals of equal energy involves no energy change and gives no spectral line: Statement (I) is false.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The molar solubility(s) of zirconium phosphate with molecular formula $\mathrm{\left(Zr^{4+}\right)_3\left(PO_4^{3-}\right)_4}$ is given by relation :
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Zr_3(PO_4)_4\rightleftharpoons3Zr^{4+}+4PO_4^{3-}}$: concentrations $3s$ and $4s$.
$K_{sp}=(3s)^3(4s)^4=27\times256\,s^7=6912\,s^7$, so $s=\left(\dfrac{K_{sp}}{6912}\right)^{1/7}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : Corrosion is an electrochemical phenomenon in which pure metal acts as an anode and impure metal as a cathode.
Statement (II) : The rate of corrosion is more in alkaline medium than in acidic medium.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Corrosion is electrochemical: the purer metal region is oxidised (anode) and the impure region, with other metal or impurities, acts as the cathode. Statement (I) is accepted as true.
$\mathrm{H^+}$ ions speed up the cathodic reduction of oxygen, so corrosion is faster in acidic, not alkaline, medium: Statement (II) is false.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I
(Partial Derivatives)		List - II
(Thermodynamic Quantity)
(A) $\left(\dfrac{\partial G}{\partial T}\right)_P$(I) $C_p$
(B) $\left(\dfrac{\partial H}{\partial T}\right)_P$(II) $-S$
(C) $\left(\dfrac{\partial G}{\partial P}\right)_T$(III) $C_v$
(D) $\left(\dfrac{\partial U}{\partial T}\right)_V$(IV) V
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
From $dG=V\,dP-S\,dT$: $\left(\dfrac{\partial G}{\partial T}\right)_P=-S$ and $\left(\dfrac{\partial G}{\partial P}\right)_T=V$.
By definition $\left(\dfrac{\partial H}{\partial T}\right)_P=C_p$ and $\left(\dfrac{\partial U}{\partial T}\right)_V=C_v$.
(A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

questions.text: Density of 3 M NaCl solution is 1.25 g/mL. The molality of the solution is :
questions.sol:
1 L of solution has mass 1250 g and contains 3 mol NaCl ($3\times58.5=175.5$ g).
Mass of water $=1074.5$ g.
Molality $=\dfrac{3}{1.0745}\approx2.79$ m.

questions.text: The species which does not undergo disproportionation reaction is :
questions.sol:
Disproportionation needs the element to be both oxidised and reduced, so it must be in an intermediate oxidation state.
In $\mathrm{ClO_4^-}$ chlorine is $+7$, its highest state, so it cannot be oxidised further and cannot disproportionate.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Consider the given figure and choose the correct option :
options: Activation energy of forward reaction is $E_1+E_2$ and product is less stable than reactant.
Activation energy of forward reaction is $E_1+E_2$ and product is more stable than reactant.
Activation energy of both forward and backward reaction is $E_1+E_2$ and reactant is more stable than product.
Activation energy of backward reaction is $E_1$ and product is more stable than reactant.
questions.sol:
$E_2$ is the rise from the reactant level to the product level and $E_1$ the rise from the product level to the peak.
Forward activation energy $=E_1+E_2$; backward activation energy $=E_1$.
The product lies higher in energy (endothermic), so it is less stable than the reactant.

questions.text:
Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their dipole moment :
HBr, $\mathrm{H_2S}$, $\mathrm{NF_3}$ and $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$
questions.sol:
Approximate dipole moments: $\mathrm{NF_3}$ 0.23 D (the lone-pair moment opposes the N-F bond moments), HBr 0.8 D, $\mathrm{H_2S}$ 0.95 D, $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ 1.0 D.
Order: $\mathrm{NF_3<HBr<H_2S<CHCl_3}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : An element in the extreme left of the periodic table forms acidic oxides.
Statement (II) : Acid is formed during the reaction between water and oxide of a reactive element present in the extreme right of the periodic table.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Elements on the far left (alkali metals) form basic oxides, e.g. $\mathrm{Na_2O+H_2O\rightarrow2NaOH}$: Statement (I) is false.
Reactive non-metals on the far right form acidic oxides, e.g. $\mathrm{Cl_2O_7+H_2O\rightarrow2HClO_4}$: Statement (II) is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text: The maximum covalency of a non-metallic group 15 element 'E' with weakest $\mathrm{E-E}$ bond is :
questions.sol:
The non-metals of group 15 are N and P. The N$-$N single bond is the weakest because of repulsion between the lone pairs on the small N atoms.
Nitrogen has no d orbitals, so its maximum covalency is 4 (as in $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Identify the homoleptic complex(es) that is/are low spin.
(A) $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_5NO]^{2-}}$
(B) $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$
(C) $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}}$
(D) $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$
(E) $\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) has two kinds of ligand, so it is not homoleptic.
(B) $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ with weak-field $\mathrm{F^-}$ and (E) $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$ with $\mathrm{H_2O}$ are high spin.
(C) $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ with $\mathrm{CN^-}$ and (D) $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ with $\mathrm{NH_3}$ are low-spin $d^6$ ($t_{2g}^6$).
Answer: (C) and (D) only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The correct order of the following complexes in terms of their crystal field stabilization energies is :
questions.sol:
Tetrahedral splitting is only about $\dfrac49$ of octahedral, so $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_4]^{2+}}$ has the least CFSE.
$\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ ($d^6$, low spin) complexes have larger $\Delta_o$ and CFSE than $\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$ ($d^7$) ones, and the chelating en gives a larger $\Delta_o$ than $\mathrm{NH_3}$.
Order: $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_4]^{2+}<[Co(NH_3)_6]^{2+}<[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}<[Co(en)_3]^{3+}}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : Nitrogen, sulphur, halogen and phosphorus present in an organic compound are detected by Lassaigne's Test.
Statement (II) : The elements present in the compound are converted from covalent form into ionic form by fusing the compound with Magnesium in Lassaigne's test.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Lassaigne's test (sodium fusion extract) is used to detect N, S, halogens and P: Statement (I) is true.
The compound is fused with sodium metal, not magnesium, to give NaCN, $\mathrm{Na_2S}$, NaX and so on: Statement (II) is false.

questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: When sec-butylcyclohexane reacts with bromine in the presence of sunlight, the major product is :
questions.note: C-1 of the ring (structure (2)) is also a tertiary carbon, so a mixture would form; NTA's final key gives structure (1).
questions.sol:
Bromination in sunlight is a free-radical substitution and is highly selective for the most stable (tertiary) radical.
The final key gives structure (1): Br on the tertiary carbon of the side chain, the carbon joined to the ring, a methyl and an ethyl group.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The most stable carbocation from the following is :
questions.sol:
All four are benzyl cations. A para methoxy group donates electrons by resonance (+R) straight into the $\mathrm{CH_2^+}$ position and stabilises it most.
A para methyl gives weaker hyperconjugative help, and a meta methoxy cannot donate by resonance (its $-I$ effect destabilises).
Most stable: the 4-methoxybenzyl cation, structure (2).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: The alkane from below having two secondary hydrogens is :
questions.sol:
Two secondary hydrogens means exactly one $\mathrm{CH_2}$ group.
2,2,3,3-Tetramethylpentane, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-C(CH_3)_2-CH_2-CH_3}$, has a single $\mathrm{CH_2}$.
The other alkanes have two or more $\mathrm{CH_2}$ groups (e.g. 2,2,4,4-tetramethylhexane has C-3 and C-5).

questions.text: The maximum number of RBr producing 2-methylbutane by above sequence of reactions is __________. (Consider the structural isomers only)
questions.sol:
The Grignard reagent RMgBr is hydrolysed to RH, so R must have the 2-methylbutane skeleton with Br on any one carbon.
2-Methylbutane has four different kinds of carbon (C-1 and the branch methyl are equivalent; C-2; C-3; C-4), giving 4 structural isomers of RBr.

questions.text:
Residue (A) + HCl(dil) $\rightarrow$ Compound (B)
Structure of residue (A) and compound (B) formed respectively is :
questions.sol:
Etard reaction: $\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2}$ in $\mathrm{CS_2}$ followed by hydrolysis oxidises toluene to benzaldehyde.
With $\mathrm{NaHSO_3}$ benzaldehyde forms the crystalline bisulphite adduct $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH(OH)SO_3Na}$, which is filtered off as residue (A).
Dilute HCl regenerates benzaldehyde (B). This is option (4).

questions.text:
Match the Compounds (List - I) with the appropriate Catalyst/Reagents (List - II) for their reduction into corresponding amines.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) An amide is reduced to an amine by $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$ then water (III).
(B) Nitrobenzene is reduced to aniline by Sn/HCl (IV).
(C) A nitrile is reduced to a primary amine by $\mathrm{H_2}$/Ni (II).
(D) The N-alkylimide releases the primary amine on hydrolysis with aqueous NaOH, as in the Gabriel synthesis (I).
(A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

questions.text: Identify the number of structure/s from the following which can be correlated to D-glyceraldehyde.
questions.sol:
A sugar belongs to the D-series when, with CHO at the top of the Fischer projection, the OH on the chiral carbon farthest from CHO points to the right.
(A) and (B): that OH is on the right, so D. (C): it is on the left, so L.
(D) is drawn with CHO at the bottom; turning it through $180^\circ$ puts CHO at the top and the lowest chiral OH on the right, so D.
Three structures: (A), (B) and (D).

questions.text:
Consider the following cases of standard enthalpy of reaction $\left(\Delta H_r^\circ\text{ in kJ mol}^{-1}\right)$
$\mathrm{C_2H_6(g)+\dfrac{7}{2}O_2(g)\rightarrow2CO_2(g)+3H_2O(l)}$ $\Delta H_1^\circ=-1550$
$\mathrm{C(graphite)+O_2(g)\rightarrow CO_2(g)}$ $\Delta H_2^\circ=-393.5$
$\mathrm{H_2(g)+\dfrac{1}{2}O_2(g)\rightarrow H_2O(l)}$ $\Delta H_3^\circ=-286$
The magnitude of $\Delta H^\circ_{f\ \mathrm{C_2H_6(g)}}$ is __________ kJ mol$^{-1}$ (Nearest integer).
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{2C+3H_2\rightarrow C_2H_6}$: $\Delta H_f^\circ=2\Delta H_2^\circ+3\Delta H_3^\circ-\Delta H_1^\circ$.
$=2(-393.5)+3(-286)+1550=-787-858+1550=-95$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
Magnitude $=95$.

questions.text: The compound with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_6H_6}$, which gives only one monobromo derivative and takes up four moles of hydrogen per mole for complete hydrogenation has __________ $\pi$ electrons.
questions.sol:
Taking up 4 mol $\mathrm{H_2}$ to reach $\mathrm{C_6H_{14}}$ means an open chain with 4 $\pi$ bonds; one monobromo derivative means all six H atoms are equivalent.
This fits hexa-2,4-diyne, $\mathrm{CH_3-C\equiv C-C\equiv C-CH_3}$: two triple bonds $=4$ $\pi$ bonds $=8$ $\pi$ electrons.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The complex of $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ ion and dimethyl glyoxime contains __________ number of Hydrogen (H) atoms.
questions.sol:
Nickel dimethylglyoximate is $\mathrm{[Ni(dmgH)_2]}$: each dimethylglyoxime ($\mathrm{C_4H_8N_2O_2}$) loses one H on binding, giving $\mathrm{C_4H_7N_2O_2^-}$.
H atoms $=2\times7=14$.
